turns.content: Elizabeth starts with 2020 switches off and must flip exactly 1993 different switches each minute. If she first has every switch on after t minutes, let c_i be the number of times switch i was flipped. What conditions do the c_i satisfy?
Use those flip conditions to determine the parity of t and derive the strongest lower bound on t obtainable from the total number of flips and bounds on the individual switch labels.
Let d_i=t-c_i be the number of minutes in which switch i is not flipped. Relate the parity and sum of the d_i to t, and check that this complementary viewpoint gives the same lower bound.
At the first duration not ruled out by that bound, each minute omits 27 switches. How many switch-minute omissions must a schedule contain in total?
Choose target non-flip counts for the minutes that have the required total, leave every switch flipped an odd number of times, and can be realized with the required omissions per minute.
Construct an explicit minute-by-minute omission schedule with those row and column totals, and explain why taking its complement gives a valid flipping schedule.
Combine the lower bound with the schedule to determine E(2020,1993), the minimum number of minutes needed to turn all the switches on.
